candidate.claim: A nonlocal difference similarity maps power eigenstates to Hurwitz-zeta functions, and evaluation at the boundary converts their spectral condition into the Riemann-zeta zero equation.
candidate.proposed_limit: The claim is spectral only after a valid closed operator domain is supplied; the source does not establish that domain.
candidate.title: Boundary quantization gives a formal Hilbert-Polya realization

parents.selection_reason: Shows that conjugating the dilation Hamiltonian by a backward difference operator reduces the eigenvalue problem to a first-order equation, while the Borel-summed inverse maps a power to the Hurwitz zeta function.
parents.title: A difference-operator similarity transform produces Hurwitz-zeta eigenfunctions

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Source-grounded mathematics, formally and on a restricted domain: the proposed Hamiltonian is conjugated by the backward-difference operator Δ=1−e^(−ip); solving the transformed first-order equation gives powers x^(−z), and a Bernoulli/Hankel calculation identifies a chosen inverse image with a Hurwitz-zeta function. Conceptual interpretation: the difference operator inserts discrete translation structure into a dilation spectrum. But Δ annihilates unit-periodic functions, so its inverse is defined only after retaining the periodic-kernel ambiguity, imposing a boundary/integration prescription at infinity, and invoking formal or Borel-summed manipulations. This is not a bounded similarity or a completed spectral theorem, and exact operator order and contour signs require the PDF.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Exposes the domain and inverse-choice data that make the formal translation-to-dilation bridge possible instead of treating similarity notation as automatic equivalence.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted after foregrounding the periodic kernel, boundary-at-infinity prescription, and formal status as required by the critic.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span defines the difference operator and its kernel, chooses decay at infinity for the inverse, develops the Bernoulli/Hankel representation, identifies the Hurwitz-zeta solution up to a periodic term, and removes that term through the eigen-equation.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The construction is explicitly formal and domain-restricted; no claim of a valid self-adjoint operator, bounded similarity, or RH result is added.

parents.title: The boundary value at zero turns the spectrum into zeta zeros

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Source-grounded mathematics: imposing ψ_z(0)=0 on the formal Hurwitz-zeta eigenfunction yields ζ(z)=0 and E=i(2z−1); the source contrasts polynomially growing trivial-zero functions with stated sublinear behavior for nontrivial-zero functions. Conceptual interpretation: evaluation at the boundary acts as a formal quantization rule, while asymptotic behavior is proposed as a domain filter. The authors propose excluding trivial-zero states on growth and later orthogonality grounds, but this span does not construct the admissible operator domain or fully justify the boundary condition, whose motivation depends on a later momentum-symmetry argument. Hence real eigenvalues are equivalent to RH only conditionally on the proposed states and domain being legitimate.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Identifies boundary evaluation as the quantization mechanism while separating formal spectral indexing from the unresolved admissibility of the states.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted after replacing definitive exclusion language with the source's conditional proposal and making the missing domain and boundary motivation explicit.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The boundary evaluation, zeta-zero condition, eigenvalue relation, trivial/nontrivial growth comparison, proposed domain exclusion, and formal RH equivalence are present despite column interleaving.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The exclusion and spectral equivalence are author-proposed and domain-conditional, not established operator-theoretic results.

parents.title: Adjoint eigenstates define a formal positive-metric inner product

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Source-grounded mathematics, conditional from the outset: assuming momentum is Hermitian on the intended domain, the authors formally compute H†, define a difference-operator metric, construct forward-difference adjoint states, and introduce a biorthogonal pairing in which integration by parts makes H symmetric. Conceptual interpretation: changing the pairing is an attempt to recast non-Hermiticity, but every adjoint and metric conclusion remains formal. Boundary terms vanish only by imposing ψ(0)=0 and pairing complementary behavior at infinity; the resulting space is explicitly not Hilbert because the proposed eigenstates have infinite norm. Positivity, invertibility, and legitimacy of the adjoint on a genuine domain are not established, and exact formulas need the PDF.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Reorders the argument by dependency, showing that the desired metric symmetry rests on the very domain and boundary assumptions it is meant to motivate.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted after foregrounding assumed momentum symmetry, boundary terms, and nonnormalizability so the representation change cannot sound conclusive.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span begins the construction under the momentum-Hermiticity assumption, gives the formal adjoint/metric and biorthogonal states, derives symmetry by integration by parts, states the boundary conditions, and says the norms diverge.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: The metric, adjoint, and Hermiticity conclusions are formal and assumption-dependent; no Hilbert-space or self-adjointness theorem is claimed.

parents.title: Distributional biorthogonality links RH to nondegeneracy and off-line zeros to Jordan blocks

accepted_interpretation.interpretation: Unproved prerequisites come first: the discussion needs a legitimate adjoint, a valid distributional domain, completeness of the proposed states, and a one-to-one boundary/secular correspondence. Under those assumptions, the authors interpret a Mellin-type integral as a delta distribution when energies are real and argue conditionally that off-critical zeros correspond to self-orthogonal exceptional points, Jordan behavior, and stronger simplicity or nondegeneracy consequences. Conceptual interpretation: biorthogonality is intended to distinguish ordinary spectral separation from exceptional-point coalescence, but the integral is not an ordinary convergent norm and the spectral-geometric language does not supply the missing framework. The row-wise column interleaving further obscures exact dependencies.
accepted_interpretation.nonparaphrase_operation: Reconstructs the dependency graph of the conditional argument and prevents exceptional-point terminology from disguising unresolved distributional and operator-domain work.
accepted_interpretation.quality_reason: Accepted after changing causal language to explicitly conditional claims and placing all missing prerequisites before the proposed consequences.
accepted_interpretation.source_support: The span displays the Mellin pairing and conditional delta interpretation, states exceptional-point and Jordan claims, and elsewhere in the same fragment names completeness and correspondence assumptions for the stronger conclusions.
accepted_interpretation.speculation_status: Jordan-block, simplicity, and nondegeneracy consequences are author arguments conditional on unproved operator and correspondence assumptions; they are not reported as established facts.
